Hi Sarah — thank you for the clear summary and the redlines. We reviewed with Legal and Security and here is a proposed approach to move toward signature quickly:

1) We attach our redlined DPA (Redwood_DPA_v3_marked.pdf) and an SCCs mapping sheet (SCCs_mapping_sheet.xlsx) that shows which SCC modules we rely on for subprocessors.

2) For international transfers we are prepared to:
   - Accept EU SCCs for controller→processor flows and provide an execution-ready UK IDTA addendum (we typically attach the Addendum as an appendix when needed).
   - Provide a concise Transfer Impact Note (1–2 pages) summarizing subprocessors, locations, and compensating measures (encryption in transit, access controls, contract commitments).

3) Subprocessor notification: we propose notification "within 30 days" for new subprocessors and the ability for customers to object with a 30-day cure period.

4) Execution: DocuSign works for us — we will prepare an envelope and share the link. If Globex prefers AdobeSign, we can accommodate but DocuSign is fastest.

Next steps: I will upload the redlined DPA + SCC map to the Drive and share the DocuSign envelope by EOD tomorrow. If you have a specific clause in your counter-redlines that you want us to address inline, please flag the page/paragraph number.

Hannah Schmitt

Subject: Re: DPA + international transfer approach (SCCs / UK IDTA)

Hi Sarah — quick note from Legal based on your counsel's asks. We can propose the following compromise language to be inserted into the DPA under "Data Transfers":

"Supplier shall enter into the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (Module 1 or 2 as applicable) for transfers from controllers in the EEA to Supplier and its subprocessors. Where a UK transfer arises, Supplier shall execute the standard UK International Data Transfer Addendum (IDTA) as an addendum to this DPA. Supplier will provide a Transfer Impact Note describing: (i) the categories of recipients and countries; (ii) safeguards applied (encryption, access restrictions, contract limits); and (iii) whether any subprocessors are located in the US and the compensating measures in place."

On notification timing: we are comfortable with a 30-day notice for new subprocessors as standard. If Globex requests a 15-day notification window, we can accept it for named critical subprocessors (e.g., analytics, logging) but cannot extend to all future subprocessors due to operational constraints. We propose to identify the subset of "security-sensitive" subprocessors in Schedule A.

DocuSign: we will prepare an envelope with the DPA + UK IDTA addendum attached and include an inline summary TIA; envelope link will be shared to this thread once ready.

Aditya Rao
Associate General Counsel, Redwood Inference
